subject: AWS Marketplace SaaS activation: entitlement mapping, evidence & go-live checklist
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightlayer.io>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: AWS Marketplace activation - evidence & entitlement questions

Hi Dev,

We're getting close to the AWS Marketplace activation window and procurement has a short list of items we need to close out before signing: 

- SOC 2 attestation (or SOC 2 in progress + interim evidence)
- Data flow diagram showing where customer data is retained/encrypted (AWS regions)
- Entitlement mapping guidance: we need the canonical mapping between BrightLayer SKUs and Redwood reportable usage units (e.g., monthly active users vs inference tokens vs seat count)
- Metering webhook spec and example payloads for aggregated vs per-tenant reporting
- A final SOW/contract for signature and the contact who will sign on Redwood's side

Can you confirm which of the above you can attach today and an expected go-live date? We have an internal procurement cutoff on 2027-08-30.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Senior Procurement Manager
BrightLayer

Attachments: BRIGHTLAYER_PO_7891.pdf (purchase order stub)
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightlayer.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace activation - evidence & entitlement questions

Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) SOC 2: We have a Type II report for 2026 attached (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf). If you need the full report portal access we can set a time for read-only access with our security team.

2) Data flow + regions: attaching a simplified data flow diagram and a short note on encryption/KMS boundaries. We host customer data in us-west-2 by default; we can discuss options for eu-west-1 if you require EU residency.

3) Entitlement mapping: see attached RW-Entitlement-Mapping-sample.csv — it contains SKU -> unit mapping and examples for common billing scenarios. Short summary: for BrightLayer we recommend mapping to a monthly-active-seat (MAS) SKU with optional per-token overage. If you prefer only seat-based billing we can enable that.

4) Metering webhook: we support both per-tenant eventing (each usage event sent with tenant_id) and aggregated daily deltas. Attached: Redwood_AWSMarketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf contains the webhook spec and example payloads. The realtime webhook sends JSON with fields: timestamp, tenant_id, sku_id, units, signature.

5) Contract & signing: copying Laura for commercial signature. We will prepare the AWS-facing SOW and route via DocuSign. Who will sign on BrightLayer's side?

Proposed go-live: if we get DocuSign back by 2027-08-28 we can schedule activation for 2027-09-03 (canary for 24 hours then full switch). If procurement needs earlier, we can accelerate.

Next actions:
- Laura will prepare the SOW and send DocuSign envelope (ETA EOD today).
- Olivia/Procurement to confirm signer and whether you need EU data residency.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: RW-Entitlement-Mapping-sample.csv, Redwood_AWSMarketplace_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf
From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@brightlayer.io>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace activation - evidence & entitlement questions

Thanks Dev — helpful. A couple quick follow-ups: 

- Signer: our VP of Finance, Mark Chen (mark.chen@brightlayer.io) will sign.
- On entitlement mapping: BrightLayer prefers seat-based billing with a token overage. Your MAS + per-token hybrid sounds right. Can you confirm the CSV has an example for hybrid billing?
- Metering granularity: procurement asked whether you can provide aggregated daily deltas only (we'd prefer that for privacy) or if per-tenant events are required for Marketplace fulfillment. Which option will AWS Marketplace require for entitlement reconciliation?
- Please include an estimated time window for the canary activation (UTC preferred).

We can review the SOW once Laura sends the DocuSign envelope.

Olivia

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace activation - evidence & entitlement questions

Hi all — looping in a quick technical-commercial note from the GTM side.

1) Entitlement mapping: the CSV that Dev attached includes a hybrid example (row 12) — seat monthly + token overage with a defined per-token multiplier for marketplace metering. Happy to walk Mark through it if needed.

2) Metering: AWS Marketplace fulfillment accepts both aggregated daily deltas and per-tenant events, but for reconciliation purposes we recommend sending per-tenant events to your backend and a daily aggregated file to the Marketplace entitlement service. That gives BrightLayer privacy (Marketplace sees only aggregates) while keeping customer-level reconciliation available between you and Redwood if needed.

3) Canary window (UTC): propose 2027-09-03 08:00-12:00 UTC for a 4-hour canary, then 2027-09-03 16:00 UTC full cutover if the canary is green. We can compress to a shorter window if you need.

4) Next operational steps: Laura will send the DocuSign for signature today; once Mark signs procurement should reply to this thread and we will raise the entitlement in AWS for BrightLayer (usually 48 hours to reflect).

Ben Carter
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference
